bot_chento_v3_v1.method: Per pool row (sorted by trigger bar t): E = t+15m, X = exit_bar_ts+15m, stop_pct = risk/entry. Production sequence: skip if E - E_last_taken < 6h (exact 6h passes; COOLDOWN_HOURS=6, strategy/config.py:143, signal.py:754, stamped at execute signal.py:1026) -> 0 skips (pool spacing is already >= 6h). BTC tilt (FILTER_NO_TILT = ASSET=='BTC', strategy/config.py:83; signal.py:407-418): skip if a TAKEN trade with kind=='stop' and R<0 has X < E and E - X <= 48h -> 10 skips, 198 taken. No halving on BTC (no TILT_HALF_AFTER_LOSS attribute; runner.py:133 getattr default False), scale=1. Sizing as botlib.size_intent_fixed_r (botlib.py:506-532) with CAPITAL_USDT=10,000, RISK_PCT=2.0, NOTIONAL_MAX_X=3.0 (config.py:15,21,22): notional_x = min(0.02/stop_pct, 3) (5 trades at cap); fixed capital, no compounding (runner.py:138). Per-trade % of capital = 100 * notional_x * stop_pct * R, with R = gross_R - cost_R and cost_R = 10bp*entry/risk, i.e. identical to 100*pnl_usdt/10,000 where pnl_usdt = price_pnl - notional*10/10000 (trades.py:341-342,356; COST_BP_RT=10.0, SLIPPAGE_BP_RT=0.0 at strategy/config.py:40,44); checked by recomputing from entry/exit_price/notional: max abs diff 3.8e-14 %. No funding: the bot closes with apply_funding=False (signal.py:504-508), so none added. Exits: stop at the stop price (R = -1 - cost_R), 6R target (TARGET_R=6.0), 72h TIF at the bar close (TIF_HOURS=72), ladder off (LADDER_ENABLED=False), OKX gate off (FILTER_OKX_ALIGNED=False, strategy/config.py:99) - all baked into the CSV R. Values rounded to 4 dp (0.0001% = $0.01); sum 290.391% = review's BTC ungated production additive total +290.391% (recon_summary KEY BTC_ungated_prod_total_return_pct_additive); count 198 matches; per-exit-year sums match the review's per-year table (2026: -6.30%).
bot_chento_v3_v1.caveats: 1) Trigger pool is a backward-only reconstruction, not the live stream: fidelity 351/357 = 0.983 of the bot's own anchors, precision 1.0 (results/fidelity_BTC.json). Its 6h cooldown runs on anchors, whereas live runs from executed entries (README.md:445-450, 887-888), so after each of the 10 tilt skips the live bot could take a trigger within 6h of the skipped one that the pool does not contain; not modelled. 2) In-sample: the chento dials (5xATR stop, 6R, 72h TIF, no-tilt, resist-OB 2R, up-30d short skip) were selected on this same history; only 6 of 198 taken trades (sum -3.38%) have t after the P1 parity cutoff 2026-07-20. The mean is therefore likely optimistic, which makes an AMBER 'worse than research' warning fire more often than its nominal 10%. 3) Non-stationary: mean by exit year 2021 +1.51, 2022 +1.85, 2023 +2.73, 2024 +1.04, 2025 +1.32, 2026 -0.18 %; the review notes BTC sits in an unrecovered drawdown since 2026-02-06, so live AMBER is plausible in the current regime without any defect. 4) Not i.i.d.: 49% of taken entries open with another same-direction position (recon_summary.txt:28), stops cluster in re-fires ~6h apart, and the 48h skip makes trade membership depend on prior outcomes. An i.i.d. bootstrap of means understates the dispersion of a live mean, so its 10th percentile is too high (warning too sensitive). 5) Heavy right skew: median -0.72%, win rate 44%, 23 targets at about +11.6..+11.9% carry the mean; small-n means are dominated by whether a target is hit. 6) BTC 48h skip memory is in-process only (signal.py:63, :697-701) and cleared by any restart; the simulation assumes no restarts, so live can take trades the baseline skipped. The live stamp is the sweep time (exit bar close + LIVE_BAR_SETTLE_S=90 s + tick), not X; no pool entry lies within 47-49h of a taken losing stop except one at 48.75h, so the boundary convention changes nothing. 7) Exact-6h cooldown ties: 16 taken entries are exactly 6h after the previous taken entry; they pass on the retry tick per code (signal.py:754 before the eval-bar stamp), but a late fill of the prior entry would drop them (tie-blocked sensitivity: 184 taken). 8) Execution model: stops fill at the stop price with no gap slippage, cost is the measured 10 bp round trip applied to entry notional at close; live TIF exit prices can differ slightly (see notes, SJ-4246). 9) Research uses snapshot bars (snapshot.db, rows < 2026-09-12); live uses the feed, which can revise bars. 10) Rows booked live before 2026-09-12 carry 18 bp (calibration log :64) and rows before 2026-09-14 08:45 bar are OKX-gated (calibration log :60-61) - neither is comparable to this gate-off 10 bp baseline.

Both counts and totals reproduce the reconciled review exactly: BTC 198 taken (10 tilt skips, 0 cooldown skips, 5 at cap), sum +290.391% vs review +290.391%; ETH 184 taken (106 halved, 0 ambiguous, 1 at cap), sum +129.957% (4-dp list sums to 129.956) vs review +129.957%. Per-exit-year sums also match the review's per-year table (BTC 2026 -6.30, ETH 2025 -8.84). The sequence and sizing came from recon.py's load/select/size, imported unchanged. Nothing was tuned. Every write went to the scratchpad (baseline_chento/). prod.db was opened read-only once, to cross-check.

Live-ledger cross-check (prod.db, read-only): the 3 distinct live BTC trades (each booked twice) were closed at 18 bp before the 2026-09-12 cost change. Re-costed to 10 bp with 100*(pnl_usdt + size_usdt*8/10000)/10000, they reproduce the research values:
- SJ-4244: 2.3458 vs research 2.3450
- SJ-4249: -2.08661 vs -2.08661 (exact)
- SJ-4246: 1.5892 vs 1.5675. Live filled its 72h time stop at 78860.54, which is above the research bar close.
Sizes match notional_x*10k exactly (for example 8611.81 = 0.86118x). So the formula 'pnl_usdt / 10,000 * 100' is the same quantity as these values.

For reference only, not a recommendation: 10th percentile of i.i.d. resampled means (20k draws, seed 0):
- BTC: n=5 -1.17, n=10 -0.42, n=20 +0.15, n=30 +0.37 %
- ETH: n=5 -1.06, n=10 -0.59, n=20 -0.21, n=30 -0.05 %

Points for whoever wires the dashboard warning:
(a) Compare only rows from the gate-off restart on, bar 2026-09-14 08:45 UTC (docs/calibration/chento_triple_v3.md:60). Earlier rows are OKX-gated, and rows closed before 2026-09-12 carry 18 bp (:64).
(b) Exclude or deduplicate the 6 double-booked 2026-08-21/22 BTC rows (3 signals x 2).
(c) The i.i.d. bootstrap understates the dispersion of a live mean, for two reasons. Trades stack in same-direction re-fires about 6h apart (about half of all entries open with another position). ETH position size depends on the previous closed trade's outcome. So the 10th-percentile threshold is too high, and AMBER will fire more often than 10% by chance. The baseline is also mostly in-sample (only 6 BTC / 2 ETH taken trades after the 2026-07-20 P1 cutoff) and non-stationary: BTC's 2026 exit-year mean is -0.18%, against +1.47% over the full period. Early AMBER on BTC is plausible without any defect.
(d) The distributions are strongly right-skewed (medians -0.72% BTC, -1.02% ETH). Means at small n depend on whether a roughly +12% 6R target hits.
